note: Histamine values from the University of Barcelona group (Vidal-Carou, Latorre-Moratalla, Comas-Basté, Sánchez-Pérez) other than Sánchez-Pérez 2018 Foods 7:205. Main source: Sánchez-Pérez et al., Nutrients 2021;13(5):1395 (CC BY, read via Europe PMC full text PMC8143338), Table 1, which reports the authors' own self-produced, updated database of Spanish-market foods (mg/kg or mg/L, mean of n samples). Plant foods in that table that overlap the 2018 paper (eggplant, spinach, tomato, pumpkin, avocado, banana, cherry, kiwi, pineapple, plum, strawberries, citrus) were left out to avoid duplicating the 2018 import; only foods the 2018 paper did not report histamine for were taken. Broad categories that don't map to one catalog food (cheese, fish, fresh/cured meat, seafood, nuts, soy-fermented products, tea, unspecified wine, red fruits) were skipped. Bread value from Hernández-Macias et al., Front Microbiol 2021 (lab-made control bread, CC BY). Red/white wine means from the Comas-Basté 2020 Biomolecules review are stored excluded because the review cites a book chapter for them. 'Not detected' = 0; beverages are mg/L converted to mg per 100 mL.
